description: Canonical list of the published test signing material and the reserved test identifiers that identity/did-usage-and-verification.md section 8 refuses on every formal verification, authorization and trust-admission path. Published material is material whose PRIVATE key ships with the specification, so a valid signature over it proves nothing about the signer. Matching is by canonicalized public-key fingerprint over algorithm-defined key material and by the typed identifier rules below; it is never inferred from the words test, fixture, did:key or example appearing in a string.
rules: published_signing_material[].fingerprint is sha256 over the ALGORITHM-DEFINED public key encoding named by public_key_encoding, never over JWK, multibase, PEM or any JSON text. The same public key carried under a different kid, DID, JWK member order or transport encoding MUST produce the same fingerprint.

Every published_signing_material row MUST declare a recomputation block naming the fixture and JSON Pointers its public key is read from, so the fingerprint is recomputable from the specification's own artifacts and a rotated fixture key turns the gate red instead of silently unbinding the obligation.

Every fixture under spec/v1/artifacts/fixtures that carries any member name in published_signing_material_field_names MUST appear in some row's source_fixtures. Publishing a new private signing key without registering it is what this rule refuses.

reserved_identifiers[] rules are independent: did, key_id and trust_domain are matched separately and by their own typed-identifier semantics. Matching one rule MUST NOT be taken to imply the others. Each row carries examples that MUST match and non_examples that MUST NOT, so the matching semantics are executable rather than described.
This registry is the only list. Domain pages, fixtures and implementations MUST NOT keep a second copy, and MUST NOT widen a rule to cover material it does not name.
Registering material here does not make unlisted material suspicious: unlisted material is still verified by the ordinary identity and trust rules.

ed25519_rfc8032_public_key.definition: RFC 8032 section 5.1.5 Ed25519 public key octet string.

p256_sec1_uncompressed_point.definition: SEC 1 v2 section 2.3.3 uncompressed point 0x04 || X || Y for the NIST P-256 curve.

mldsa65_fips204_public_key.definition: NIST FIPS 204 ML-DSA-65 public key byte string.

recomputation_schemes.jwk_okp_x_b64u: One pointer to the base64url OKP x member; the decoded bytes are the public key.
recomputation_schemes.jwk_ec_uncompressed_point_b64u: Two pointers, x then y, each base64url; the public key is 0x04 || X || Y.
recomputation_schemes.raw_public_key_b64u: One pointer to the base64url encoding of the algorithm-defined public key bytes.

published_signing_material.why: Ed25519 key generated from the published fixed seed bytes 0x00 through 0x1f. It signs the Ed25519 detached-JWS KAT, the franking proof transcript, the KeyPackage write transcript, the recovery transcript and the producer signer KAT, so every one of those fixtures hands a verifier a working private key.
NIST P-256 key derived from the same published seed bytes as the Ed25519 row. It signs the ES256 detached-JWS KAT.
ML-DSA-65 key whose 32-byte FIPS 204 generation seed is published alongside it, so the signing key is reproducible by anyone. It signs the post-quantum raw detached-signature KAT.

The RFC 8032 section 7.1 TEST 1 Ed25519 key. It is the proof-of-possession key of the WebSocket DPoP known-answer test, and its private key has been published in an IETF document since 2017; a holder of this key can mint a syntactically perfect DPoP proof.

reserved_identifiers.why: Every DID the conformance artifacts sign under is a did:webvh whose SCID segment is hand-written rather than derived. A real webvh SCID is a base58btc digest and a real did:key multibase ed25519 value starts z6Mk with a capital M, so a lowercase z6mkfixture or z6mkagent SCID cannot collide with material a deployment actually produced.

The fixture verification methods end their fragment with -fixture. The rule matches the fragment alone, so re-hanging a fixture key id under a deployment DID is still refused. Fragments such as runtime-1 that do not carry the suffix are covered only by the DID rule, which is why the three rules are evaluated independently.

Trust domains are compared as the value of the ak:trust_domain typed identifier, never as a DNS suffix of an arbitrary string. Registered values cover the bare conformance token; the reserved top label rule covers the RFC 2606 and RFC 6761 names the fixtures use, which no deployment may claim.
